Shortwave radio is an enjoyable, inexpensive hobby, because one is able to listen to foreign broadcasts, and learn of world events in real time, before modern news outlets are able to report on it. For example, the fall of the USSR was broadcasted in real time over shortwave. In addition one can listen to thousands of amateur radio operators (hams) from around the world on shortwave radio. I have listened to a ham in Australia make contact to a ham in America. Many, but not all amateur radio operators started off by listening in on shortwave. I know that's how I got started! Moreover, there is a great thrill one gets when your homebrew receiver picks up that foreign broadcast, or that ham radio operator far, far away. There are many aspects of shortwave radio that excite me. For example, I run a very old receiver I got off of Ebay. I have listen to many hams and broadcasts on that rig. I hope you find this post informative and helpful. Checkout the sidebar for related sites and feel free to post a question or two. Also, any shortwave listeners should feel free to comment as to what they get out of the hobby.

My father collects antique radios. This is a Bendix 526, the pride of his collection.

This radio when we last checked was worth over $900. The reason for it's worth is the scarcity of the plastic it is made from. It's called catalin plastic. During WWII due to manufacturing products for military use, plastic became scarce and more expensive to use in civilian manufacturing. Many companies decided to mix the colors to make their production quotas. Today almost all radios made from catalin are worth inordinate amounts of money. If you find one for under $100, BUY IT! You will see a big return on your investment.
